correctness.rationale: Use the run containing the physical origin to fix both the derivative index and the level in the roof tower. This gives a conjugacy over the binary symbol-flip extension with roof y_0; the extension has zero relative entropy and every derivative invariant measure lifts. The variational and return-time entropy formulas therefore give h_k=sup h_mu/(1+mu([2])). The no-three-ones restriction gives mu([2])≥1/3, and an MME (which exists for the finite-alphabet subshift) symmetrized under symbol interchange has mu([2])=1/2 without loss of entropy. Together with the Fibonacci base this proves the bounds. With triple letters excluded, three singleton runs are precisely the middle three letters of an alternating five-block, and three double runs are precisely the two listed six-blocks. The reconstructed 14-state graph gives the stated determinant, indexed periodic counts, and an everywhere positive 15th power. The positive Perron vector descends to the complement quotient, whose only positive eigenvalue solves the displayed quartic; primitivity implies mixing and uniqueness of the Parry MME.
residual_risks: The exact graph certificate is only for depth two; all-depth inequalities rely on the tower argument. The stated constants are bounds, not asserted optimal or equal to the actual contraction ratios.

value.rationale: The derivative hierarchy is a natural interpolation between a positive-entropy finite-type shift and the infinitely differentiable Kolakoski shift. The explicit comparison quantifies complexity loss when passing from derivative time to spatial time. Depth two is the first shift with nontrivial derivative restrictions; its exact graph invariant gives all periodic counts, mixing and a computable entropy rather than just a finite search for short periods.
residual_risks: No higher-depth zeta classification or resolution of the classical Kolakoski word conjectures is implied.
